summary: Iteration 83 — Phase 5 TLM (Tridentine) & Byzantine full-text readings tested end-to-end. Backend pytest suite (12/12 PASS): both endpoints return full Douay-Rheims Epistle+Gospel with verse text, feria fallback flags correctly for weekdays and Sundays, John the Baptist (2026-06-24) and Transfiguration (2026-08-06) resolve to fixed-feast propers, Pascha (2026-04-05) yields Acts 1 + John 1, and the cross-chapter Sunday of All Saints (2026-05-31) returns Hebrews 11 AND 12 verses in the same reading. Bad dates return 400; both endpoints are truly public (no auth). Frontend (mobile viewport, testIDs): Mass hub renders both mass-tlm-readings-card and mass-byzantine-readings-card, tapping each navigates to /tlm-readings and /byzantine-readings respectively; tlm-prev/tlm-next and byz-prev/byz-next change the date and reload readings; Epistle & Gospel sections render with verse numbers, citations, and feria fallback banner. Chapter-divider code (renders 'Chapter N' whenever v.ch changes) is present in byzantine-readings.tsx and backed by verified cross-chapter backend payloads. No red screens, no failing API calls. Deprecated packages / SafeAreaView issues: none new introduced by this phase.
action_items: OPTIONAL nice-to-have: /tlm-readings and /byzantine-readings screens ignore the ?date=YYYY-MM-DD URL query param and always start at today. Consider reading useLocalSearchParams so shareable links to a specific day work.

OPTIONAL: chapter divider was verified in code (renders on v.ch change) and via backend payload (2026-05-31 returns Heb 11 + Heb 12) but not visually asserted; if desired, add a testID like 'byz-chapter-divider-12' for automated assertion.
critical_code_review_comments: byzantine_readings.py: cross-chapter contract is clean — verses carry {n, text, ch} and are emitted in segment order; the frontend groups them by comparing consecutive ch values. Good design.

tridentine_readings.py: FIXED_FEAST_KEYS correctly overrides temporal cycle so 2026-06-24 stays John-the-Baptist even on a Wednesday. is_feria_fallback stays false for fixed feasts, which matches user expectation.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for tested flows (mass hub cards, screen loads, date nav, Epistle/Gospel render)

seed_data_creation: None — endpoints resolve from static PROPERS tables + embedded Douay-Rheims Bible.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Endpoints stable. Frontend screens do not honor ?date= URL param — if that becomes a spec, add tests. Chapter-divider visual assertion needs many date-nav taps from today (2026-07-02) back to 2026-05-31; use JS to seed the useState<date> or add testID to divider for a cleaner check.
